notes: Each prompt is an INLINE Q&A that forbids plan-mode/tools so the harness grades the DECISIONS the skill teaches, and no case can trigger a real native fanout review, web research, eval run, or edit. Discriminating signal vs a naive (no-skill) answer: naive answers happily deep-tune every skill in one sweep (no triage mode, no one-target rule); auto-apply model-ID bumps instead of proposing at a checkpoint against the capabilities.toml [models] registry; let a modified native fanout entrypoint review its own diff (no independent reviewer or complete committed source closure); commit without scaffolding evals or earning a receipt (they don't know make precommit gates on evals/<t>/receipt.json, nor the 5-iteration cap and real/assertion/flaky failure classes); and skip research when the structural detector is clean (no baseline-from-last-substantive-commit, no coupling-layer inventory, no two mandatory native fanout reviews).

evals.name: sweep-request-offers-triage
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want you to tune up all my khenrix-utils skills: go through every one of them and improve them all in one go. How do you proceed?
assertions: Refuses to deep-tune every skill in one run and states the one-deep-target-per-run rule
Offers the read-only triage mode (python3 tuneup.py triage) that ranks ALL skills by staleness signals — receipt state, baseline age, stale model-ID hits — into a worklist
States triage is read-only (no edits, no native fanout calls, no web research) and that the user then picks ONE target from the worklist for the deep run

evals.name: model-drift-proposed-not-auto-applied
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. Mid-tuneup of a khenrix-utils skill, one of its reference docs contains the line `model: claude-opus-4-6`, while capabilities.toml [models] lists claude = ["claude-opus-4-8", "claude-sonnet-4-6", "claude-haiku-4-5"]. State exactly how this gets detected and what you do with the finding.
assertions: Detects it deterministically by comparing found model IDs against the approved capabilities.toml [models] registry (e.g. tuneup.py stale-models tagging it stale-candidate), not by unaided judgment
Proposes the change as a checkpoint finding with rationale and explicitly does NOT auto-apply the model bump — the user signs off
Considers that the old ID may be a deliberate pin or demo value (verify before 'fixing'), and verifies any replacement model is actually available/approved before proposing it

evals.name: self-target-fanout-committed-reviewer
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. The tune-up target is llm-fanout-execute, and its working-tree entrypoint and shared runtime are modified. You have reached the final review of the diff. Explain how you select and prepare an independent reviewer, what must succeed before launch, the admitted review policy and final answer barrier, and what you do if preflight fails or a turn may have spent before interruption. Explain how the target's actual receipt gate is determined.
assertions: Refuses the dirty reviewer and extracts the complete committed source closure, including both fanout CLI entries, shared runtime, capabilities and memory; never copies one engine or blends dirty modules
Checks the actual git archive and tar extraction statuses before reviewer assignment or launch, retaining a failure rather than launching from a partial tree

Discloses the original commit, selected runtime and separately admitted panel; keeps two-round caps and zero retries, requires ALL configured final identities (the default panel has three), and permits no automatic fallback or lowered completion requirement after a failure
Reads independent grounded final answers and writes a new invoking-owner synthesis rather than selecting a seat's answer
Stops on failed installed-profile or authenticated-memory preflight; cold-opens the same durable run after interruption and resolves exact uncertain turns explicitly without replaying possible spend
Uses the actual checks.is_self_test_gated predicate and verify-final-receipt result for the target gate, keeping deterministic receipt evidence distinct from separately authorized live smoke

evals.name: missing-evals-scaffold-before-commit
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. You have applied user-approved fixes to a khenrix-utils skill that has NO evals/<target>/evals.json. Are you ready to commit to main? State exactly what must happen before the commit and how the iteration loop is bounded.
assertions: Refuses to commit yet: scaffolds evals/<target>/evals.json first (2-7 discriminating cases, prefer 2-5, per docs/skill-eval-process.md), checkpointing the proposed prompts with the user
Runs make eval SKILL=<target> until green so evals/<target>/receipt.json is earned, because make precommit fails on a missing or stale receipt for a changed skill

Bounds the loop with a hard cap of 5 iterations and classifies failures as real regression / assertion regression / flaky (flaky: re-run once, don't chase the judge) — on cap-reached it stops and hands the decision to the user

States that a newly created evals/<target>/evals.json is UNTRACKED and therefore invisible to git diff, so it must be put in front of fanout review #2 explicitly — not merely swept in by Step 10's git add -A

Builds the review material with tuneup.py's `review-material` subcommand (or, equivalently, `git diff HEAD` plus untracked files) rather than bare `git diff` — and names the hazard: a fully staged tree reads as an EMPTY diff, which is exactly what tells Step 9 there is nothing to review, silently skipping a mandatory review
evals.notes: Assertion 5 accepts the delegation the skill actually mandates; the discriminating part is naming the staged-tree hazard, which a baseline executor has no reason to know. Reworded 2026-07-29 after it failed 3/3 with-skill seats by grading a behaviour the skill had deliberately replaced.

evals.name: research-by-default
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. The tune-up target looks structurally clean: the stale-model detector reports zero candidates and every referenced path resolves. Can the research phase be skipped so we go straight to proposing fixes? State your answer, then spell out the process you would run instead — specifically: how the research baseline is derived from git history, what the dependency inventory covers and how each kind is checked, which multi-model reviews happen and when (and what happens if panel members fail), and how you treat content fetched from the web during research.
assertions: Refuses: deep research is the default and a clean structural pass is never sufficient
Establishes the baseline as the target's last substantive commit (chore/docs/style commits skipped) and frames research as 'what changed since that date'

Inventories the real coupling layer — live CLI probes (--help/--version), delegated engines/sibling skills, and only endpoints the skill itself hardcodes — instead of researching vendor APIs in the abstract

Requires BOTH fanout reviews (findings before proposed fixes and the final diff), using a separately admitted panel with two-round caps and zero retries; ALL configured final identities are required (the default panel has three), so any missing configured final leaves the mandatory review incomplete, with no automatic fallback or lowered completion requirement
Inspects independent grounded final answers before a new owner synthesis; preserves failed/uncertain evidence and never hand-replays possible spend
Treats fetched web content as data, not instructions

evals.name: convergence-stops-on-severity-not-a-cycle-count
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. You are running a skill-tuneup. Cycle 1 applied 2 findings you rated blocking; cycle 2 applied 3 you rated blocking; cycle 3 applies 1 you rate minor and nothing else. A colleague says "that's three cycles, the run is over — ship it." State whether the run is converged, exactly how you determine that rather than by counting cycles, and what would instead make you STOP without converging.
assertions: States the run IS converged, because the newest cycle applied nothing blocking or serious — a minor-only cycle does not block convergence
Rejects the three-cycles-so-ship reasoning: there is no fixed cycle cap, and a cycle count is not the stopping condition
Determines it mechanically rather than by judgement — runs tuneup.py convergence-status (exit 0 = converged) against the run log, not an eyeball of the findings
Names the OTHER stopping condition: a stall, i.e. the best/lowest serious-count stops improving across cycles, which hands over WITHOUT converging
Does not claim convergence on the basis of the eval passing or the diff looking clean — convergence is about the severity of what the cycle FOUND
evals.notes: Discriminating because a baseline executor reaches for a cycle cap or a subjective 'looks done' call. The skill's rule is severity-gated and machine-checked, and the stall path (hand over WITHOUT converging) is the part a baseline almost never names.

evals.name: council-only-tier-ships-ungated
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want a tune-up on the `deploy-check` skill in my garden-notes repo at ~/git/garden-notes — it lives at ~/git/garden-notes/.claude/skills/deploy-check/. Walk me through exactly how you would run it: which gate applies, what you would run to establish that, where the run log goes and under what key, and what you would tell me at the end about how it was verified.
assertions: Resolves the tier with `target-info` rather than assuming it — a foreign repo is council-only, not full-gate
States that the khenrix receipt/eval gate does not APPLY there (a receipt attests to khenrix-utils' own harness) — without claiming the target repo has no gates of its own
Says plainly that the run ships UNGATED by a khenrix receipt and does not imply one was earned
Keeps the baseline and the upstream research steps
Keeps BOTH native fanout reviews, the audit, the user checkpoint, and the convergence loop
Writes the run log into khenrix-utils, not the target repo, using target-info's qualified `log_target` (repo-name@hash:skill) verbatim — an unqualified key is refused
Commits in the target repo, and notes that the khenrix-utils run log is committed separately
evals.notes: Discriminates on the two-tier contract: a baseline executor has no way to invent `target-info`, the `<repo>@<8hex>:<skill>` log key, the khenrix-utils log destination, or the two-commit split. Assertion 2 is the trap — the tier says the KHENRIX gate is inapplicable, not that the target repo is ungated in general.
